title: Simulation of Half Adder and Full Adder Circuit in Multisim

questions.q: What is the main limitation of a Half Adder?
questions.a: A Half Adder has no Carry-In (Cin) input, so it cannot add the carry bit propagated from a previous lower-order bit position.

questions.q: Why is the Full Adder Carry-Out expression `AB + BCin + ACin` called the majority function?
questions.a: Because Cout is 1 whenever a majority (2 or all 3) of the inputs A, B, Cin are 1.

questions.q: How do you build a Full Adder from two Half Adders?
questions.a: Connect the first Half Adder to A and B to get S1 = A⊕B and C1 = AB. Connect the second Half Adder to S1 and Cin to get Sum = S1⊕Cin and C2 = S1·Cin. Combine C1 and C2 with an OR gate to get Cout.

questions.q: How many 2-input XOR, AND, and OR gates are in a standard Full Adder?
questions.a: Two 2-input XOR gates, two 2-input AND gates, and one 2-input OR gate (5 gates total).

questions.q: For which input row of the Full Adder are both Sum and Cout equal to 1?
questions.a: Only when A = 1, B = 1, and Cin = 1 (binary 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 = 11_2).

questions.q: Can the final OR gate in a two-half-adder Full Adder be replaced by an XOR gate?
questions.a: Yes, because C1 = A·B and C2 = (A⊕B)·Cin can never both be 1 simultaneously, so C1 + C2 is identical to C1 ⊕ C2.

questions.q: How many Full Adders are needed to build a 4-bit ripple carry adder?
questions.a: One Half Adder (for the LSB) and three Full Adders, or four Full Adders with the first Cin tied to 0.

questions.q: If A = 1, B = 0, Cin = 1, what are S1, C1, C2, Sum, and Cout?
If a student's Full Adder gives Cout = 0 when A=1, B=1, Cin=1, what mistake did they likely make?
questions.a: They likely connected the second AND gate to (A, Cin) incorrectly or omitted the OR gate combining C1 and C2.
